strings.name: Angela Merkel
strings.role: Former German chancellor · European crisis management
strings.summary: Merkel moved from scientific research in East Germany into politics and became Germany’s first female chancellor, serving for sixteen years. She played a central role in the euro crisis, refugee reception, the energy transition and the pandemic response. Her negotiating style shaped European politics, while austerity, migration policy and reliance on Russian energy remain contested parts of her legacy.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected milestones do not constitute an exhaustive record of all news or controversies.
strings.influence.rationale: Her long chancellorship and responses to financial, euro-area and refugee crises profoundly influenced European governance.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Coordinating European crises
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Participated in euro-area rescue measures and policy coordination, shaping European economic and political choices.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Long tenure, contested policies
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Four terms encompassed refugee reception and the energy transition; their costs and consequences remain debated.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Continued public debate
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Discussed the EU, democracy and her political role at the European Forum.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Published Freedom
strings.timeline.event-02.text: With long-time aide Beate Baumann, reflected on her life and government from 1954 to 2021.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Left the chancellorship
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Olaf Scholz succeeded her after four terms beginning in 2005.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Refugee policy turning point
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Germany received large numbers of asylum seekers, generating both support and divisions within society and her party.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Became chancellor
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Became Germany’s first female chancellor and subsequently led several coalition governments.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Led the CDU
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Took over the Christian Democratic Union and later led the parliamentary opposition.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Entered the Bundestag
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Elected after German reunification; joined the federal cabinet in 1991 and later became environment minister.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Completed her doctorate
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Conducted quantum chemistry research at East Germany’s Academy of Sciences.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Born in Hamburg
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Moved to East Germany with her family as an infant and grew up in Templin.
